proofs.text: In a git checkout, run `--all --record --commit`; verify `Record committed as developer.`, that the record's `commit` differs from HEAD because the record's own commit came after it, and that the rule's state is `Recorded`. Change the scoped file `src/feat.py` and commit it; verify the rule's state is `Tested`

reasons: PROOF-20 happy_path_only: No proof of this rule names a rejection, an error or a boundary.
rule_text: A record carries the git tree hash of its feature's scoped files, so a rule stays Recorded while only other files change and falls back to Tested when a scoped file changes

tests.body:
def test_verify_then_sync_status_shows_the_rule_recorded(self, tmp_path):
        root = _pytest_project(tmp_path)
        (root / 'src').mkdir()
        (root / 'src' / 'feat.py').write_text('VALUE = 2\n', encoding='utf-8')
        _spec(root, 'feat')
        _git_repo(root)

        before = _rule_state(root, 'feat', 'RULE-1')
        assert before == 'Drafted', before

        code, out = _run(root, '--all', '--record', '--commit')
        assert code == 0, out
        assert 'Record committed as developer.' in out, out

        record = _newest_record(root, 'feat')
        assert isinstance(record['scope_tree'], str), record['scope_tree']
        assert record['proofs'][0]['id'] == 'PROOF-1'
        assert record['proofs'][0]['status'] == 'pass'
        assert record['feature'] == 'feat'
        assert record['gate'] == 'tested'

        # The record is one commit behind HEAD, which is the case the scope
        # tree exists to cover.
        assert record['commit'] != _head(root)
        assert _rule_state(root, 'feat', 'RULE-1') == 'Recorded'
tests.name: test_a_rule_falls_back_to_tested_when_the_scope_changed
